name: Merritt Hart
episode: The missing name on the stern
life: “I still remember being taught to say my customer's name while checking an invoice.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Merritt by a small Monday habit. Merritt looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I thought I was hiring a painter. The apprentice taught me to say the owner's name without flattening the last sound.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a sand-colored linen shirt and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Merritt has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a loose dark braid. Merritt takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Merritt has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To pronounce the marine customer's name correctly.
family: Hank Fry is Merritt’s second cousin. Merritt is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Hank calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, Hank says, “I sell lighthouse cards printed inland. I asked the crew to show me their view from the bunk.”
connections: Amanda Quintero. A flag maker and a bookkeeper practice the spoken name before they put it in different alphabets.
